title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 10th District
area: Central and western North Carolina, including all of Catawba, Iredell, Lincoln, and Yadkin counties and most of Forsyth County, including much of Winston-Salem.

context.text: Incumbent Pat Harrigan defeated a single Republican primary challenger. Ashley Bell won a six-way Democratic primary with 47.3% of the vote.

summary.text: Pat Harrigan is the Republican incumbent for North Carolina's 10th Congressional District, a West Point graduate and former Army Special Forces officer who co-owns firearms-industry businesses. He lost the 2022 race for the 14th District to Democrat Jeff Jackson, then won the open 10th District seat in 2024. According to his House website, he is focused on national security and accountability in government.

background.text: Born in San Diego, California, in 1987.
Earned a degree in nuclear engineering from the United States Military Academy at West Point in 2009.

Commissioned as an Infantry officer after West Point and served at Fort Wainwright, Alaska, according to his House website; deployed to Afghanistan as a platoon leader, then volunteered for and earned the Green Beret and returned to Afghanistan with Army Special Forces. He was awarded two Bronze Stars.
Served in the U.S. Army from 2009 to 2014.

Began a small firearms business at home with his wife, Rocky, in 2015 while still on active duty, per his survey; he co-owns ZRODelta, UnBrandedAR, and US Optics, which he says now operate from a 120,000-square-foot facility employing more than 50 people.
Ran in 2022 for the 14th District, losing the general election to Democrat Jeff Jackson, 57.7 percent to 42.3 percent.

Won the 2024 Republican primary for the open 10th District seat with 41.2 percent over Grey Mills Jr. (38.9 percent) and others, and the general election with 57.5 percent over Democrat Ralph Scott Jr. (38.2 percent), Libertarian Steven Feldman, and Constitution Party candidate Todd Helm; took office January 3, 2025.

Serves on the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (Energy Subcommittee; Investigations and Oversight Subcommittee) and the House Committee on Armed Services (Intelligence and Special Operations Subcommittee; Military Personnel Subcommittee; Readiness Subcommittee) for the 2025-2026 Congress.
According to his House website, he has been married to Rocky since 2010, and they have two daughters, Reagan and McKinley.

priorities.text: In his 2022 campaign survey, said he was focused on curbing inflation, cutting spending, and pursuing an all-of-the-above domestic energy strategy including oil exploration, pipelines, fracking, nuclear, solar, wind, and coal.
priorities.quote: I'm passionate about ending inflation and getting our economy back on track. That includes an aggressive approach to an all-of-the-above energy strategy that makes America energy independent.

priorities.text: In the same survey, said he was passionate about securing the border, addressing illegal immigration, protecting the Second Amendment, and election integrity.
priorities.quote: I'm also passionate about securing the border, dealing with our illegal immigration problem, protecting the 2nd Amendment, and election integrity.

positions.summary: In an April 2025 statement on the House vote, said the SAVE Act, which requires proof of citizenship to register to vote, keeps elections limited to citizens.
positions.quote: Our elections are for American citizens, and the SAVE Act makes sure it stays that way

positions.summary: In 2026 statements on Iran war powers resolutions, said the administration had complied with the War Powers Resolution and that he opposed forcing a withdrawal, while also calling for stronger congressional engagement and saying his vote was not an endorsement of continued action without congressional involvement.
positions.quote: It is not a blank check, and it is not an endorsement of continued action without congressional involvement.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology and the House Committee on Armed Services for the 2025-2026 Congress.

candidates.name: Ashley Bell
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 47.3% of the vote over five challengers.

summary.text: Ashley Bell is the Democratic nominee for North Carolina's 10th Congressional District, a physician assistant and educator who describes herself as not a career politician. A Texas native, she trained as a physician assistant at Wake Forest and has taught in public schools and at the university level. She is running on health care, education, and cost-of-living issues.

background.text: Born in Tyler, Texas, and graduated from Henderson High School; she says she was raised in rural East Texas by small-business owners and was the first in her family to attend college.

Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Houston (2003), a graduate degree from Wake Forest University School of Medicine (2011), and a graduate degree from the University of Lynchburg (2019); according to her campaign website, the latter is a Doctor of Medical Science.
According to her campaign website, she began her career as a junior high and high school band director in Texas before moving into medicine.

Works as a physician assistant; according to her campaign website, she has about 15 years of clinical experience in emergency medicine, primary care, rural clinics, and telemedicine in North Carolina.
Works as an educator; her campaign website describes about 20 years in education, including as a public school teacher and a university professor teaching physician assistant students.

Says she served on national boards and committees in her profession; Ballotpedia lists affiliations with the American Academy of Physician Associates, the Physician Assistant Education Association, the American Association of University Professors, and Democratic Women of North Carolina.
Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 47.3 percent of the vote; she has not previously held elected office. According to her campaign website, she lives and works in the Triad.

priorities.text: Says the cost of health care, rent, and housing has become unaffordable while billionaires prosper, and wants to outlaw prior authorization requirements by insurers.
priorities.quote: Everything is too expensive... People can't afford rent, or to buy homes... Prior authorization MUST be outlawed.

priorities.text: Lists saving democracy, affordability, Medicare for All, and public education funding among her policy priorities.
priorities.quote: Saving Democracy, Affordability, Medicare for All, Public Education funding and access, Affordable Higher Education, Disability Rights, Women's Rights, Human Rights

positions.summary: Supports Medicare for All and outlawing insurer prior-authorization requirements, drawing on her experience as a physician assistant treating patients who can't afford medication or mental health care.
positions.quote: Medicare For All. This is the goal.

positions.summary: Her campaign site calls for codifying a woman's right to choose and opposes abortion restrictions and bans.
positions.quote: Codify a woman's right to choose.

positions.summary: Her campaign site calls for a $17 per hour national minimum wage with cost-of-living adjustments.
positions.quote: $17/hour National Minimum Wage with cost of living scale adjustments

positions.summary: Her campaign site calls for abolishing ICE and replacing it with a new immigration enforcement system, while saying the country still needs immigration enforcement and reform.
positions.quote: Not only should we abolish ICE, but we should hold those who beat, murdered and enabled these crimes accountable.

positions.summary: Her campaign site lists gun reform among the additional policies she supports while also saying she supports the Second Amendment.
positions.quote: Common sense gun reform. We support the 2nd amendment, but we don't support gun violence.

positions.summary: Her campaign site lists the Green New Deal, including a transition to clean, renewable energy, among her policies.
positions.quote: Green New Deal. Transition to clean, renewable energy; public transit expansion, increase jobs in clean energy and manufacturing, decreases pollution.

positions.summary: Her campaign site calls for repealing legislation such as the SAVE Act, which she says imposes unfair requirements on voters.
positions.quote: Recent legislation (like the SAVE Act) imposes unfair and unnecessary requirements that disproportionately impact women.

positions.summary: Her campaign site lists recognizing Palestinian statehood and stopping funding for Israel's military actions among her policies.
positions.quote: Recognize Palestinian Statehood and stop funding Israel's attacks.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says that taxing billionaires appropriately, along with ending spending on ICE, would pay for Medicare for All.
positions.quote: If we tax billionaires appropriately and stop spending billions on a paramilitary domestic terrorism force called ICE, we can afford it easily.

candidates.name: Steven Feldman

summary.text: Steven Feldman is the Libertarian Party candidate for North Carolina's 10th Congressional District and a physician and medical scientist who is a professor at Wake Forest University. He was also the Libertarian candidate in the district in 2024, when he received 2.9 percent of the vote. According to his campaign website, he is running to promote individual liberty, reduce federal debt, and support international peace.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he has lived in North Carolina for more than 40 years and received his medical training at Duke University and the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill; WFAE reports he received his M.D. and Ph.D. from Duke University School of Medicine.

Works as a physician and medical scientist; WFAE reports he is a professor of dermatology, pathology, and public health sciences at Wake Forest University and a senior advisor at Sensal Health, and he describes himself as having been rated one of the world's leading dermatology experts.
Was the Libertarian nominee for the 10th District in 2024, receiving 2.9 percent (11,614 votes) in a race won by Pat Harrigan.
According to his campaign website, he and his wife, Leora, have been married for 40 years and have two sons.

priorities.text: Lists fiscal responsibility among the public policy areas he is passionate about.
priorities.quote: Fiscal responsibility. We shouldn’t leave our children a country deeply in debt.

priorities.text: Lists peace among the public policy areas he is passionate about.
priorities.quote: Peace. War is immoral, counterproductive, & costly.

priorities.text: Lists individual liberty among the public policy areas he is passionate about.
priorities.quote: Individual liberty. Let people do what they want but not hurt others.

positions.summary: Says he agrees with part of both the pro-choice and pro-life positions, and lists making abortion illegal after a certain period of gestation, keeping government out of funding abortions, and letting states adopt different rules.
positions.quote: Making abortion illegal after a certain period of gestation, with proper consideration for the health of the mother

statements.quote: The government should NOT take guns away from law-abiding citizens.
Some people advocate Medicare for all. This is a great idea, as long as it’s paid for. Let’s allow people who want Medicare to pay the premium and use Medicare.
We have seen, though, that a policy based solely on blocking people at the border is, like our failed drug war, costly and ineffective.
We can expect the power of the market to continue to drive new responses. Government should encourage, but not attempt to direct, these responses.
The question of who gets to participate in which sports is not going to bankrupt our country or cause the collapse of our nation.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from Feldman's campaign website (My Positions page) and his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. His abortion answer is recorded as mixed because he says he agrees with elements of both sides. Nothing was found on rent regulation, minimum wage, tariffs, school choice, police funding, or war powers.
